title: Fluorescence Imaging Reveals Heterogeneous Water Structuring and Protein Organization in Liquid−Liquid Phase Separation
authors: Sara Anselmo; Federica Scollo; Elisa Bonaccorso; Giuseppe Sancataldo; Giovanna d’Angelo; Luca Lanzanò; Valeria Vetri
abstract: Abstract Water is increasingly recognized as an active thermodynamic component of liquid−liquid phase separation, whose local organization and dynamics regulate phase behavior by modulating intermolecular interactions, solvent entropy, and the stability of condensed phases. Here, we combine micro-Raman spectroscopy with phasor-based spectral imaging and fluorescence lifetime analysis of environment-sensitive probes to map solvent-dependent changes across coexisting phases at the sub-microscale. Complementary observables reporting on solvent dipolar relaxation, local protein environment, phase partitioning, and hydrogen-bond organization converge to a consistent picture of local hydration. Our results reveal distinct hydration states in the coexisting phases: the protein-rich phase displays reduced dipolar relaxation, consistent with a more constrained hydration state than the PEG-rich phase, and these signatures remain associated with the phase composition across different conditions. Furthermore, the multimodal approach identifies substantial local heterogeneity within both phases and an interfacial microenvironment with physicochemical properties distinct from those of the coexisting bulk phases, demonstrating that LLPS generates spatially heterogeneous microenvironments rather than homogeneous compartments. Overall, this work provides a spatially resolved view of hydration heterogeneity in LLPS and establishes a broadly applicable strategy for investigating hydration and local physicochemical organization in biomolecular condensates and other phase-separated soft matter systems.
